    "category": "ReDoS",
    "message": "The new validation bounds pattern length but does not guard against catastrophic backtracking. For example, `^(a+)+$` with flag `g` passes validation, and executing it against `'a'.repeat(40) + '!'` also passes the inline-code limit. The engine then calls native `regex.exec` synchronously without a time budget, allowing exponential backtracking to block the event loop and make the MCP server unresponsive. The claimed ReDoS protection needs a linear-time regex engine, unsafe-pattern rejection, or isolated execution with an enforceable timeout."

    "severity": "high",
    "category": "Unbounded file read",
    "message": "The new path-size guard trusts `stats.size`, but the handler accepts special files and subsequently performs an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` through `src/utils/fileUtils.ts` (HEAD lines 51–52). On Unix, `{ \"path\": \"/dev/zero\" }` passes the existence check and reports a size of zero, then continuously supplies bytes to the read until resource exhaustion or read failure. Thus the 500,000-byte cap can be bypassed even when no custom rules are installed. Reject non-regular files and bound the actual read to the limit plus one byte; a bounded read also protects against files growing between `stat` and `readFile`."
  }

    "message": "Reusing the Statistics object does not preserve a consistent snapshot. StatisticsLoaderThread passes the DataManager's Note objects into Statistics without copying them, while MonthChart recalculates daily counts from those objects whenever the dialog is constructed or its filters change. If a retained note is edited between visits, the monthly heatmap reflects its changed text while the cached overview totals, yearly/weekly counts and phrases remain unchanged. Snapshot the note data or cache the daily aggregates as well so all tabs represent the same statistics until refresh."

    "category": "Asynchronous state ownership",
    "message": "A cancellation callback clears the shared cache and loading flag without checking whether its loader is still active. StatisticsLoaderThread can emit cancellation twice: chunkComplete() emits it when the user cancels, but run() continues waiting for the worker futures and emits it again if a remaining worker subsequently fails. If the user starts a replacement load between those events, the obsolete callback marks that replacement idle or erases its completed cache, permitting overlapping loads and out-of-order publication. Associate callbacks with an active loader or generation and ignore obsolete callbacks."
